Just so people are aware (and if they didn't read the whole article), many of the limits on free speech today fall into specific categories, like lying under oath (perjury), specifically trying to get a person killed, intentionally lying about someone to try to harm them (libel / slander) etc.

Freedom of speech was intended to protect political statements, not to protect anything that could possibly come out of your mouth. Thus in a sane and civilized society, there must be a few limits placed on specific types of speech, while still doing our best to ensure that speech that avoids such harms is protected... and merely being offended, or disagreeing with an idea does not mean you are being harmed by it.

And of course this doesn't go into the difference between your right to say something free of government coercion or consequence... and that of a private institution or individual not allowing you to use their property to promote your message. So while a KKK or Neo-nazi group has the right to hold a public protest on public property, they don't have a right to force a private establishment to let them hold their rally there. But lest we go down that rabbit hole... I'll leave it at that. But we might want to talk about things like "free speech zones", "gay wedding cakes", etc...

The article does a good job of summing this up, but I fear that many here might merely be waving the "free speech" banner of "anything goes" without actually reading the article and understanding that it makes clear that certain types of speech are not, and should not, be free. But it does protect the right to say things that are merely offensive... even incredibly offensive... so long as they fall into that category of protected speech that it describes.
